title: Conditions for Buying, Selling or Gifting a House in Vietnam 2026
desc: What a house must meet to be sold or gifted under Article 160 of the 2023 Housing Law: certificate, no dispute, no seizure, no land recovery decision.
summary: The conditions the house and the parties must meet before a sale or gift under Articles 160 and 161 of the 2023 Housing Law, with the contract, notarization and title transfer steps.
body: p

Before paying a deposit to buy a house or drawing up a deed gifting a house to a child, many people ask only "is there a certificate yet?". In fact, Article 160 of Housing Law No. 27/2023/QH15 (effective from 1 August 2024) sets more conditions. This article summarizes those conditions, with links to the original text.
h2
1. Which transactions must meet the conditions?
p

Housing transactions include sale, lease-purchase, lease, gift, exchange, inheritance, mortgage, capital contribution, lending, free accommodation, and authorization to manage a house (Article 159). Among these, sale, lease-purchase, gift, exchange, mortgage and capital contribution of a house must meet all the house conditions in Clause 1, Article 160.
h2
2. The five conditions for the house in a sale or gift
p
Under Clause 1, Article 160, the house must:
ol
Have a certificate (sổ đỏ, sổ hồng) as required, except in the cases in section 3 below;
Not be subject to a dispute, complaint or lawsuit about ownership;
Be within the ownership term, if it is a house with a fixed-term ownership;
Not be seized to enforce a judgment or a legally effective administrative decision; and not be subject to provisional emergency measures or preventive measures of the Court or a competent authority;
Not be covered by a land recovery decision or a notice of clearance or demolition of the house from a competent authority.
p

Because a house is attached to land, when selling or gifting a house together with land use rights, the land must also meet the conditions in Article 45 of the Land Law 2024: a certificate, land not in dispute (or the dispute resolved), land use rights not seized, land use term still running, and no provisional emergency measures applied.
h2
3. Cases where a certificate is not required
p
Under Clause 2, Article 160, a house does not need a certificate when:
ul
Selling, lease-purchasing or mortgaging a house to be formed in the future; selling a house upon dissolution or bankruptcy;
An organization gives away charity houses, compassion houses or great solidarity houses;

Selling or lease-purchasing ready-built houses of a project investor that are public property housing, social housing, housing for the people's armed forces, or resettlement housing that is not public property;
Leasing, lending, free accommodation or authorization to manage a house; receiving a house by inheritance.
p

In those cases, substitute documents are required under Article 8 of Decree 95/2024/ND-CP. For example, selling a house to be formed in the future that is not part of a project requires land use right documents and a building permit (where a permit is required). Note: a gift of a house between individuals is not on this list, so a certificate is still required.
h2
4. Conditions for the seller, buyer and recipient of a gift
ul
The seller or donor must meet the capacity conditions under civil law (Clause 1, Article 161).
A domestic individual buyer or recipient of a gift is not required to have residence registration where the house is located (Point a, Clause 2, Article 161).
Foreign individuals and overseas Vietnamese must be among those allowed to own housing in Vietnam; overseas Vietnamese must also comply with the Land Law (Point b, Clause 2, Article 161).
h2
5. Rented houses and co-owned houses
ul

Selling a rented house: the tenant must be notified in writing; the tenant has priority to buy if all rent has been paid. If the tenant does not buy within 30 days of receiving the notice, the owner may sell to another person, unless otherwise agreed (Article 168).

Gifting a rented house: the tenant must be notified in writing at least 30 days in advance; the tenant may continue renting until the contract expires, unless otherwise agreed (Clause 2, Article 177).

A house under joint ownership in common as an undivided whole (usually spouses, or a whole family named together): a gift requires the written consent of all owners; for co-ownership by shares, each person may gift only their own share (Clause 1, Article 177).
h2
6. Steps to carry out
ol
Check the certificate, any dispute, seizure, planning and land recovery status of the house before paying a deposit.

Prepare a written contract with the content required by Article 163: information on the parties, features of the house and land plot, price, payment method, handover time, rights and obligations of the parties, etc.

Notarize at a notarial practice organization or authenticate at the commune-level People's Committee where the house is located; a sale or gift contract takes effect from the time notarization or authentication is completed (Clauses 1 and 4, Article 164).

One party files the application for a new certificate (title transfer); if receiving the house together with residential land use rights, the competent authority recognizes both house ownership and land use rights for the recipient at the same time (Clauses 2 and 3, Article 162).
Declare and pay taxes and the registration fee as required. See also Land and house registration fee 2026.
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal documents. The 2023 Housing Law, Decree 95/2024/ND-CP and the 2024 Land Law have had some articles amended; Law No. 04/2026/QH16 amending the Law on Notarization is not yet in force (from 1 January 2027). When transacting, check the current documents and ask the notary organization and the People's Committee of the commune or ward where the house is located.
